metadata.note: Hub topology: mega-sync seeds (3631300, 589aece, 0dca5bf, 3247b10) create a 25-seed connected component via hard xrepo edges. Groups split at sync-commit boundaries to respect 2-5 size constraint while maximizing intra-group xrepo coverage.

groups.rationale: Mirror tonic 0.14/prost 0.14 upgrades across qdrant contract and rust-client. Both are layer-0 foundation commits — 9c0248c has 65 descendants (highest in workspace), 4c4e356 has 8. No hard xrepo edge detected (independent framework upgrades), but identical semantic purpose and shared generated qdrant.rs hotspot.
xrepo_edges_cross_group: 9c0248c descendants feed into G02/G03/G04 qdrant seeds
4c4e356 descendants feed into G02/G04 rust-client syncs

groups.rationale: Core v1.19 contract features (TurboQuant, memory placement, IDF corpus) paired with their primary SDK sync commits. Hard xrepo: e58be0c→589aece, ad3abf7→3631300, ad3abf7→589aece, 76f4f3e→3631300, 76f4f3e→589aece. 3631300 and 589aece are mega-sync hubs consuming many features — grouped here with the highest-impact v1.19 contract changes they consume.

Filter/search contract changes and their SDK consumption. 2573869 (keyword prefix) and 55cf6b7 (slice filtering) extend filter vocabulary; 73e6c16 (remove deprecated search) is breaking API change. 5ffa732 and 693c6a3 are direct SDK consumers. Hard xrepo within: 55cf6b7→693c6a3, 73e6c16→5ffa732, 55cf6b7→5ffa732. High DAG co-occurrence: 2573869 (55 desc), 55cf6b7 (37 desc), 73e6c16 (36 desc).

BM25/text search pipeline (disabled stemmer, TextQuery) plus id tracker memory placement, paired with their SDK syncs (0dca5bf for rust-client, 3247b10 for python). Hard xrepo within: 08a73b5→0dca5bf, 8a5566c→0dca5bf, 9614dc0→0dca5bf, 9614dc0→3247b10, 8a5566c→3247b10. These represent the 'next wave' of features after v1.19 sync.

Resource management lifecycle: d75d805 introduces strict mode max_disk_usage_percent (layer 0, 39 desc), c34acc1 supersedes it with global quota API (layer 1, 38 desc), da58e7d removes the field in python client. Hard xrepo: c34acc1→da58e7d, d75d805→da58e7d. 7477c7c (stale snapshot fix) is a cluster stability fix with hard xrepo to 589aece(G02); placed here as it shares the operational/stability theme.

Filter/index extensions: bedab3c (substring match), fb0cda7 (nested payload indexes), 7f44c40 (nested payload sync in rust-client), de3c432 (text/phrase local mode fix). Hard xrepo: bedab3c→de3c432 (substring contract consumed by local mode fix). fb0cda7→7f44c40 is soft (conf 0.6) but they're a semantic mirror (same author within 3 days). High affinity: all extend the filter/index vocabulary.

Serverless client prototype — entirely new product track across both SDKs. d5a4f44 (rust serverless, +1871 LoC, layer 2) seeds 8c14f9f (pagination, +399 LoC, layer 3). 7e917d1 (python serverless, +3660 LoC, layer 3) is the largest addition in qdrant-client. All three create new modules (src/serverless/ and qdrant_client/serverless/). Intra-repo DAG: d5a4f44→8c14f9f. Cross-SDK parallel development.

Python local mode correctness campaign. 53c81ee opens the filter correctness hardening (layer 0, 25 desc). f28634c (layer 0, 32 desc — highest in qdrant-client) is the philosophical shift to warning about dropped params. f212c4a starts fail-fast semantics for empty vectors. 5c0fd88 fixes shared-state mutation in collection config. 1860632 replaces asserts with proper validation. All in qdrant-client local mode paths. Payload_filters.py is the hotspot (41 revisions).
xrepo_edges_cross_group: ad3abf7(G02)→5c0fd88 (hard, memory placement consumed in config isolation)
73e6c16(G03)→1860632 (hard, deprecated search terms used in validation)

groups.rationale: Low-affinity seeds with no hard xrepo edges to other seeds. d4b0466 (rust-client connection check, standalone feature). b09b213 (python remove deprecated add/query, net -1322 LoC). f7530a2 (nested json-path parser, new utility module). d6f79fd (sparse vector isolation, new sparse.py module). 789eced (gRPC conversion performance). Each is self-contained or starts a distinct sub-theme. Grouped for batch processing efficiency.
